title: Dioramas

description.main: The first volume in the Damiani and Matsumoto Editions series on Hiroshi Sugimoto, devoted to the Dioramas he has photographed in natural history museums since 1974. Fifty-six black-and-white plates made between 1976 and 2012, arranged as a history of life on earth, with a text by the artist. Clothbound, 118 pages.
description.extended:
Hiroshi Sugimoto's Dioramas opens the series of books on his work that Damiani began with Matsumoto Editions in 2014. It is the first book devoted to the series that opened his career.

Sugimoto began photographing natural history dioramas in 1974, soon after moving to New York. He had noticed that the tableaux at the American Museum of Natural History looked real when he viewed them with one eye closed. He photographs them with a large-format camera, framed to leave out the glass and labels. Taxidermied animals and painted backdrops read as living scenes. The book gathers 56 black-and-white plates made between 1976 and 2012. It sequences them as a history of life on earth, from prehistoric sea creatures to early humans and on to a world without people. Sugimoto wrote the text. The title page records that the book accompanied Hiroshi Sugimoto: Still Life at Pace Gallery, New York, in May and June 2014. Clothbound, 118 pages.

Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) has worked between Tokyo and New York since the 1970s. His long series test what a photograph can record. Seascapes and Theaters followed as the second and third volumes in this set. He has described photography as a fossilization of time, and the Dioramas apply that idea to scenes that were never alive.
description.artist_bio: Hiroshi Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) moved to New York in 1974 and divides his time between Tokyo and New York. His work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo, the National Gallery London, the National Museum of Modern Art Tokyo, the Smithsonian and Tate (per Artbook/D.A.P.). The Dioramas series, begun 1974 after a visit to the American Museum of Natural History, was his first major body of work.
description.exhibition_context: Per the Getty catalogue record the title page states the book accompanied Hiroshi Sugimoto: Still Life, Pace Gallery, 510 West 25th Street, New York, May 9 to June 28, 2014, which included Polar Bear (1976) and later Dioramas up to 2012.

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Damiani / Matsumoto Editions series. First volume in the series (Seascapes 2015, Theaters 2016). Title page states the book accompanied Hiroshi Sugimoto: Still Life at Pace Gallery, New York, May 9 to June 28, 2014; the Getty record gives the imprint as Pace Gallery in association with Damiani. Damiani lists release June 2014; the US release through Artbook/D.A.P. was September 2014. 56 black-and-white plates.
